databricks.overrideDatabricksConfigFile.description: Override location of .databrickscfg file (default: DATABRICKS_CONFIG_FILE environment variable or ~/.databrickscfg)

databricks.overrideDatabricksCLIPath.description: Override location for the Databricks CLI (defaults to the CLI bundled with this extension). *Warning:* it is recommended NOT to set this. If you override the CLI to an outdated version this extension may break.

databricks.clusters.onlyShowAccessibleCl.description: Enable/disable filtering for only accessible compute (compute on which the current user can run code)

enumDescriptions: Show cluster view in the explorer.

databricks.notebooks.configureJupyterCel.description: Automatically configure Jupyter cell markers in workspace settings for Databricks Python notebooks. Disable in User settings to leave Jupyter cell markers unchanged. Reload the window after changing this setting. Previously written settings are not removed.

databricks.wsfs.rearrangeCells.description: Enable/disable rearranging cells in wrapper files created when using `workspace` as the sync destination. **Note:** It is recommended to NOT disable this setting. If you do disable it, you will need to manually handle sys.path for local imports in your notebooks.

databricks.connect.progress.markdownDescription: Show PySpark progress bar when using Databricks Connect. Requires `ipywidgets` package and `pyspark@3.5.0+`.

databricks.connect.serverlessDbconnectVe.markdownDescription: Default `databricks-connect` version for serverless compute. Determines required Python version and suggested package version. Minimum supported value is `15.4`.

databricks.ipythonDir.description: Absolute path to a directory for storing IPython files. Defaults to IPYTHONDIR environment variable (if set) or ~/.ipython.

enumDescriptions: Automatically set up a uv-managed Python environment matched to your Databricks compute for suitable uv projects.
Never run automated Python environment setup; use your own interpreter and environment (for example an existing `.venv` with `databricks-connect`) as-is.
databricks.python.environmentSetup.markdownDescription: Controls the extension's automated Python environment setup for uv projects. `auto` (default) offers and runs uv-native setup (`databricks environments setup-local`) for suitable projects. `manual` disables it entirely so your existing interpreter/environment is used as-is — useful when your network blocks `raw.githubusercontent.com`, which the automated setup requires to fetch runtime constraints.

databricks.proxy.strictSSL.markdownDescription: Controls whether TLS certificates are verified for the extension's Databricks SDK calls. No longer used.
databricks.proxy.strictSSL.markdownDeprecationMessage: No longer used. The extension now follows `#http.proxyStrictSSL#` for TLS certificate verification.

databricks.proxy.caCert.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a PEM bundle of additional CA certificates. No longer used.
databricks.proxy.caCert.markdownDeprecationMessage: No longer used. The extension's Databricks calls now use VS Code's certificate handling, which adds the OS trust store when `#http.systemCertificates#` is on. Install the CA in the OS trust store, or start VS Code with the `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` environment variable set to the PEM bundle's path.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Databricks
walkthroughs.description: Connect, explore data, use Databricks models, run code, and deploy.

steps.title: Connect to your workspace
steps.description:
Sign in once, and every Databricks view uses that workspace. Use a profile you already have, or sign in with your browser.
[Setup authentication](https://docs.databricks.com/dev-tools/vscode-ext/authentication) describes the options.
[Sign in](command:databricks.connection.configureLogin)

steps.title: Explore your data
steps.description:
Browse catalogs, schemas, tables and volumes in the Unity Catalog view, and open a table's columns and details without leaving the editor. Your workspace files are in the Workspace file system view.
[Open Unity Catalog](command:unityCatalogView.focus)

steps.title: Chat with Databricks models
steps.description:
The models your workspace serves through Unity Gateway show up in Chat, agent mode included. Pick one in Chat's model picker.
[Choose a Databricks model](command:databricks.unityGateway.chooseModel)

steps.title: Give your coding agent Databricks skills
steps.description:
AI tools add Databricks skills to Copilot, Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, so your agent knows how to work with your workspace's jobs, pipelines and data.
[Install AI tools](command:databricks.aitools.install)

steps.title: Work directly on Databricks compute
steps.description:
Start an SSH tunnel to open a VS Code window that runs on serverless compute or your cluster, with your workspace files and the compute's Python environment.
[SSH tunnel](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/ssh-tunnel) describes how the tunnel works.
[Start SSH tunnel](command:databricks.ssh.startTunnel)

steps.title: Deploy jobs and pipelines
steps.description:
A bundle is a folder whose databricks.yml describes its jobs and pipelines. Create one from a template, then deploy and run it from the Project view.
[Declarative Automation Bundles](https://docs.databricks.com/dev-tools/vscode-ext/bundles) explain the details.
[Create a new project](command:databricks.bundle.initNewProject)

viewsWelcome.contents: Sign in to use your Databricks workspace in VS Code, and Databricks models in VS Code Chat.
Sign in to use your Databricks workspace in VS Code.
This window signs in with the SSH tunnel's credentials, and they don't connect. If the session's token expired, close this window and start the tunnel again from a local window.

To learn more about how to use the Databricks extension for Visual Studio Code [read our docs](https://docs.databricks.com/dev-tools/vscode-ext.html) or [Quickstart guide](command:databricks.quickstart.open)
The guides for this extension, such as how to run files and deploy bundles, are in the [User Guide](https://docs.databricks.com/dev-tools/vscode-ext.html).

Connect your IDE to a Databricks SSH tunnel so you can run all Python and SQL workloads using Databricks compute.
[Start SSH tunnel](command:databricks.ssh.startTunnel)
To learn more about the SSH tunnel [read our docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/ssh-tunnel).

Connect your IDE to a Databricks SSH tunnel so you can run all Python and SQL workloads using Databricks compute.
[Start SSH tunnel](command:databricks.ssh.startTunnel)
To learn more about the SSH tunnel [read our docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/ssh-tunnel).

Choose a Databricks project from a subfolder of the open folder:
[Choose a project](command:databricks.bundle.selectActiveProjectFolder)

This folder has a Databricks project configuration (.databricks/project.json) from an older version of the extension. The extension now works with Declarative Automation Bundles and no longer migrates these projects.
[Learn how to migrate](https://docs.databricks.com/dev-tools/vscode-ext/bundles)

No bundle (databricks.yml) was found in the open folder or its subfolders, except hidden folders and node_modules. To use one elsewhere, pick its folder:
[Select a project](command:databricks.bundle.selectActiveProjectFolder)
